verdict: sql/038_transport_companies.sql is, line for line, close to the best file in this repo: box-drawing banner, honest STATUS block, a per-bullet security review that names the attack rather than the measure, a published limit-of-the-guarantee section ending in 'Do not read this file as claiming otherwise', rejected designs costed in place (auto-refund on 'lost', recording blocked dispatches as 'refused' rows, refusing vs clamping an over-ceiling tariff, inlining the definer helper back into policies), dead hooks labelled as dead, and a verify block whose negative assertions include the one that catches the most likely future mistake (a balance column appearing on an append-only ledger). Its cross-file provenance is real, not invented: I checked the sql/015 r9 postmortem, sql/023's wallet_charge signature and column order, and the index.html citations at the commit the file was written against (playerOwnsVehicle 195441, the TW-vs-economy_nodes id postmortem 206493, the 'does not exist' comment 79921, PP_COND_MULT 195340) - all four were exact then and have since drifted ~250 lines because index.html grew in the same commit. I applied the file three times in a row with ON_ERROR_STOP against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster with auth/wallet_charge stubs: no error on any run, and the verify returned exactly the numbers on its own '-- Expect:' line (tables 5, policies 7, helper 1, rpcs 5, secdef 6, guards 2, and 0 for every negative assertion). The RLS boundary holds under test: as authenticated, UPDATE on companies and rigs, INSERT into the ledger and contracts, and SELECT on config all returned 'permission denied for table ...', and a rig INSERT carrying runs_used = 9 was refused by trg_ins. But the file does not win, because it overstates its own guarantee twice and one of those overstatements is a live, ratified-decision-breaking exploit that I reproduced end to end.
biggest_gap: The Meridian price ceiling is computed from an unclamped, unbounded, attacker-populated median, and the Meridian branch of transport_quote returns before the max_price_per_contract check. Fix both: clamp each row's base to v_cfg.max_tariff_per_unit_hop inside the percentile_cont (and/or restrict tco_ins so a charter cannot be INSERTed with a tariff above the config ceiling, plus bound charters per owner), and move the over_price_cap guard above the `if p_carrier_id is null then return` early exit so it covers the NPC quote as well. Then either enforce max_fleet_rigs at rig registration or delete both it and the 'fleet size' word from the header's list of things that are capped.
evidence:
MEASURED on a throwaway PG16 cluster (initdb 16.13, auth.users/auth.uid/wallet_charge stubs, Supabase's blanket grants pre-applied), file applied 3x clean, verify row: tables 5 | policies 7 | helper 1 | rpcs 5 | secdef 6 | guards 2 | no_rig_upd 0 | no_co_upd 0 | no_ledger_write 0 | no_cfg_pol 0 | ledger_balance_cols 0 | cfg_rows 1 - exactly the '-- Expect:' line.

(1) MERIDIAN CEILING IS ATTACKER-CONTROLLED. sql/038:754-758 computes the median over the RAW stored tariff: `select percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by (c.tariff->>'base')::numeric) ... where c.status='open'`. It is never clamped to max_tariff_per_unit_hop (500). tco_ins (:537-541) pins owner_id/status/reliability/blacklist but NOT tariff, and the structural CHECK (:232-237) allows base up to 100000, and nothing caps charters per owner. Reproduced as `authenticated`: with one honest carrier at base 20, `transport_quote(null,'N-25','N-26',1,1,false)` returned price 50. After 20 free `insert into transport_companies (owner_id,name,tariff) values (auth.uid(), 'Shell n', '{"base":100000}')` - no depot, no rig, no Cinder - the same call returned {"ok":true,"carrier":"meridian","price":250000}. One player raised the NPC price ceiling ~5000x for every other player. That is the exact failure ratified decision (b) exists to prevent, and it falsifies the file's own comment at :751-753: "Median rather than mean so one carrier posting an absurd sheet cannot drag the ceiling up for everybody."

(2) THE MERIDIAN BRANCH SKIPS max_price_per_contract. The early return at sql/038:769-779 fires before the `over_price_cap` guard at :831-835, so the cap is enforced on player quotes only. Measured: `transport_quote(null,'N-25','N-26',6,50,false)` returned {"ok":true,"price":75000000} against max_price_per_contract 5000000, and `transport_dispatch(null,null,'N-25','N-26',6,50,'{}',false,'big-1')` returned ok:true with price 75000000 and the stub wallet went 200000000 -> 125000000. A 75,000,000 Cinder charge, 15x the file's own ceiling - whose 5,000,000 default carries a sourced provenance comment at :441-444 citing sql/034's measured 1,000,000 largest-ever credit. This needs no exploit at all: set_sheet legitimately clamps base to 500, so an honest market median of ~67 already puts a max-size Meridian haul (5000 units x 6 hops) over the cap. It also falsifies the header's SECURITY REVIEW bullet at :136-137 ("price - ... refused above max_price_per_contract") and the §4.2 comment at :944-947 ("a route the board would not quote is a route this cannot dispatch").

(3) A COMMENT ASSERTS A RULE THE CODE DOES NOT ENFORCE. Header :147-148: "Every one of those is capped (fleet size, runs, hops, units, price)." max_fleet_rigs appears only three times (sql/038:446, :464, :1491) and the third is a value echoed back in transport_set_sheet's jsonb - it is never enforced. Reproduced: transport_set_sheet returned "fleet_cap": 12, then a single `insert into transport_rigs ... from generate_series(1,40)` registered 40 rigs, all with the SAME vehicle_id, all rarity 'mythic', condition 'Pristine', runs_cap 10, all accepted by trg_ins. There is no unique index on (company_id, vehicle_id) and no per-owner charter bound either. The per-rig daily run limit that :1011-1026 defends at length as a fraud lever is therefore bypassable by registering more rows.
